recipes.name: Jalapeño Cream Cheese Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
2 jalapeno peppers, seeded and minced (wear gloves)
8 ounces shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Season chicken breasts with 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, 1 teaspoon cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper; place in a baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until chicken is no longer pink inside and juices run clear, 30 to 35 minutes. Cool chicken, then shred with two forks. Set aside.

Heat butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add onion and jalapeños; cook until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in cream cheese; cook until melted. Stir in remaining 3 teaspoons garlic powder, remaining 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, paprika, chili powder, and cumin. Stir in shredded chicken; remove from heat.

Pour 1/2 enchilada sauce in bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Lay tortillas on a work surface; spoon chicken mixture in a line across center of each tortilla. Sprinkle each with about 1 tablespoon Monterey Jack cheese. Roll up tortillas; place in sauce in the dish, seam-sides down. Pour remaining 1/2 sauce over enchiladas. Sprinkle remaining 4 ounces cheese over top.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is hot and bubbly and cheese has melted, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Jalapeño Cream Cheese Chicken Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: This jalapeño cream cheese chicken enchiladas recipe yields creamy green chile enchiladas with shredded chicken and spicy jalapeños baked with cheese.

video.description: These Jalapeño Cream Cheese Chicken Enchiladas are vibrant and bursting with flavors. The creaminess of the cheese mixed in with garlic, cayenne pepper, chili powder, and cumin brightens and gives the enchiladas a depth of flavor. Use green or red sauce to top, along with Monterrey Jack cheese! Bake in the oven, and you’ll have a wonderfully flavorful meal.

review.reviewBody: Add what you want and make this recipe yours! I used chicken, mushrooms and spinach in the filling. I also used half green chile and red enchilada sauce. Poured it right in the pan and it actually looked as fabulous as it tasted. I did prefer the green sauce better but both were good. I'll try shredded beef or pork with green chili sauce and a dash of sour cream next time.

One of my new favorites. I threw the filling ingredients into my Instant Pot with the breasts still frozen - skipped the butter. Pressure cooked on high for 30 minutes and released pressure naturally. Spooned into the tortillas, topped with shredded cheddar, then put in the oven for a few minutes to melt the cheese. Easy, fast, and delicious!

I usually use fresh Hatch or canned green chilies without all the extra spices added as I've made this dish for my kids who are now all in their 40s. It's a tradition in our home on Christmas Eve. I use enough of each large can green enchilada sauce (mild) to cover the bottom of the one time use trays I'm using. The rest of the can of sauce goes in with the brick of cream cheese, the 2 cups of mixed Mexican blend shredded cheese, the chilies (chopped), diced onions, and whatever protein source you are using. Mix well. I soften my tortillas (can use corn or flour) in the microwave or oven and then fill with 1-2 tbsp. of the mixed ingredients and roll without closing ends. I can normally get at least a dozen or so in each pan. I top with more enchilada sauce, chopped or sliced olives, and more cheese and pass cilantro, sour cream, and salsa around at the table. - mscmiranda

Had to use corn tortillas because they are gluten free and used rotisserie chicken. I added frozen, thawed and drained spinach as well as a can of drained black beans to up the nutrition. If you are using corn tortillas, be sure to warm them a bit (I minute in the microwave for the whole package.) I dipped the tortillas into the enchilada sauce before I rolled them. Very forgiving recipe that allows you to make changes and still come out delicious!

One major thing missing: you need to heat the tortillas before filling and rolling them or they tear. Wrap in a damp kitchen towel or paper towel and microwave for 30 seconds for much better (rip-free) results. Also, the cream cheese is too thick once melted. I needed olive oil in addition to the butter plus some cream and water to thin the sauce out enough to spread top and bottom in the pan. It is too cream cheese-flavored. I prefer it more as an actual jalapeño cream sauce, not a Philly version of enchiladas.

The hubs says this is fantastic.I seasoned the chicken and cooked it in an instant pot and doubled the cream cheese and seasoning for the peppers.Instead of the green I used red enchilada sauce. 
The instant pot made this a quick and tasty dinner.

This was sooooo good. I cooked the chicken the day before use my sous vide cooker so it was really tender. Saved a little time making it tonight. Used a variety of peppers saved from my garden instead of the 2 jalapenos. Definitely saving this recipe.

So good even though I totally cheated!!! I have tried multiple enchilada recipes through the years and none of them turned out. Until this one! I used rotisserie chicken breast. I didn’t use butter but rather just sautéed onion and about 1.5 to 2 tblsp jar diced jalapeño in cooking spray. Then I added the cream cheese and melted it a little and added chicken and second set of spices. I used hot pepper cheese shredded cheese. I did use green enchilada sauce. Perfectly spicy and yummy. Absolutely a keeper and will make many times. Thanks for a great recipe!
Fantastic~ Used Costco rotisserie chicken, thawed and chopped...added more cream cheese and used whole wheat tortillas... Its fantastic...make a double batch and freeze the second pan!!
Outstanding recipe! I use one large poblano pepper and a small can of green chili. I know this will be my go-to recipe from now on!

These are a decent amount of work but they’re sooo good and super flavorful! The dish has a nice creamy element and also tastes super fresh with the veggies and green sauce. It was also kinda spicy with the cayenne and peppers, but I wasn’t too careful about removing the seeds from the jalapeños. The chicken was a little overdone; I think baking at 35 minutes would be enough for my oven, especially since you put the enchiladas back into the oven for 35 min at the end. I also like the idea of using rotisserie chicken. I would definitely make these again as they were a huge hit in this household!

Those look more like burritos than enchiladas. I tried this recipe using traditional corn tortillas. I used 12 corn tortillas, or 2 enchiladas per serving, Quite tasty, although the baked chicken was kind of tough.
This was so good and fun to make! I only used 5 large burrito shells, but it was still a ton of food. The flavor is absolutely amazing. Definitely add your jalapeno according to your own taste!!

I felt this was too creamy. It would be better if it had some sort of texture in the tortilla filling. I also think that corn tortillas would be better. It was good. Just not great. But still a good recipe.
My family loved these!!!!

I’ve made this recipe multiple times now and I think it’s safe to say I love it. I’m so grateful to this beautiful person for sharing this. It’s so easy and soooo incredibly delicious!! No changes from me, 10/10
I toss in hot green chili's and use a store rotisserie chicken.
Was able to make my own chili verde from all fresh ingredients from the garden instead of canned enchilada sauce. But the seasonings and rest of the recipe was perfect!

This is the BEST!! I have made this several time for family dinners and will always be my go to recipe for enchiladas. You can be very creative with this recipe You can make it as individual enchiladas as written or as a casserole which you can add different ingredients like black beans, refried beans, Spanish rice and so much more. And, I'm not trying to change the recipe just switching things up, when you use this awesome recipe as much as I do. And the people that complain about changing the recipe and not following it to the exact. Who says they don't do that in the beginning enjoy the recipe and want to switch things up. That's what you call creative minds. So the people that don't like to be creative and go with the exact recipe. Boring! Start thinking outside the box people!
I absolutely love these nothing need to be changed however I like more spice so I added extra jalapeños to mine.
